answer: A trellis of mutual endorsements can keep an agent economy honest: an identity earns its place on the trellis only when established agents vouch for real completed work, and those endorsements decay if the vouched agent misbehaves. A newcomer starts out like an onyx pebble, opaque and untrusted, with no history to spend. Spinning up a thousand sybils means growing a thousand separate trellises from nothing, each needing genuine work before it can transact, while rewards stay capped per identity. Crossing that dune of upfront effort costs an attacker far more than the fake identities are worth.
